rationale: Fold the third confirmed result, and one reading-derived protection, back into the implementation map. The configuration-change behavior no longer asks whether an adopted unpersisted configuration can be committed, because the executed check with its accepted correspondence review observed exactly that; the FSM-application behavior replaces its unanswered question about a rolled-back configuration with the sourced relationship that only committed entries reach the FSM and committed entries are not truncated, keeping the reading-derived part visible as a residual.

b-config-change.rationale: Replace the answered premise with its sourced conditional relationship: a node holding an adopted configuration continues to campaign under it because latestIndex differs from committedIndex, a fresh peer with an empty configuration can supply the missing vote, and the leader commit path promotes the adopted configuration to committed once its index falls within the commit index without consulting the entry stored at that index. Only the restart question remains open.
b-config-change.preserves: b-config-change keeps its owner, trigger, configuration coordinate and its edges to f-config-membership and f-commit-quorum; the confirmed durability finding and the confirmed committed-configuration finding both rest on the same leader-side publish path, and the readout behavior is unaffected.

b-fsm-apply.rationale: Replace the unanswered question about a configuration entry applied while its latest configuration was rolled back: the FSM receives only entries that processLogs admits up to the commit index, and a committed entry is not removed by the follower's conflict truncation because an elected leader must be at least as up-to-date as a majority of the previous configuration, so the rollback that does exist applies to the uncommitted latest configuration and not to the applied one. The residual states that this chain is a reading argument.

feedback.answered: Two propositions. First, a node that adopted an unpersisted configuration can later commit it: in a two-node run the adoption was followed by a campaign under the adopted voter set, the fresh peer's vote supplied the majority, the node returned to the leader state, and its committed configuration then contained two voters at an index whose log entry is a LogNoop while the peer's own configuration held a single voter. Second, a configuration that has been applied to the FSM cannot be rolled back by a truncation of the latest configuration, because the FSM only receives entries admitted up to the commit index and a committed entry is not truncated under the election restriction; the rollback path in the follower append handler applies to the uncommitted latest configuration.
remaining: Whether a committed configuration with no supporting entry survives a restart and is re-derived from the log (b-config-change).

Whether the election restriction always keeps truncation above every committed configuration index, and whether the (setState, setCurrentTerm) pair can be observed as a term regression under an off-thread heartbeat (b-fsm-apply, b-follower-append).

Whether treating an unsupported pre-vote response as granted can let a partitioned candidate believe it would win (b-prevote), and whether TimeoutNow is validated against sender or term (b-leadership-transfer); both are bounded by the real-vote quorum but unexamined by execution.

Whether any caller outside this repository depends on the configuration index reported by GetConfiguration (b-config-readout), and whether the majority-intersection reasoning covers every permitted one-at-a-time change sequence (b-commit-quorum).
feedback.rationale: The consequence premise is answered at measured granularity by an executed check whose correspondence review was accepted, so the behavior records the confirmed relationship and only the restart question stays open. The FSM-application answer is a reading argument over the commit bound and the election restriction, so it is recorded as a protection with its residual gap named rather than as an established result. The three confirmed findings and the untouched frontier items are retained for separate questions.
